BOPEN.heard: Building virtual environments exam prep, key terms, go-dough, unity, and unreal. Thirty-four ideas, each with its name and go-dough, unity and unreal, from scenes and signals to clocks, collision, units, and licenses. Knowing each engine's exact word lets you port a game idea and instruct an agent precisely.

BIDEA.heard: Hollow, this is Lai'am in for bear. People moving from Godot to Unity often say a node is a component, not quite. A Godot node is one object, like a Unity game object, where Unity adds components, Godot uses a node type and child nodes. The Unity and Unreal names come from their documentation, not from runs. This film goes through the terms, each one shown with all three names.

BDEFS.heard: Four labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow. In the book text, the course text uses and explains the term. Computed, the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs. Simulation, a model run step by step from stated rules, not a measurement of a real game. Conceptual, a drawing of the idea with no data behind it.

B0101.heard: This table is the map 34 terms, each one idea with three engine names, GoDoh, Unity, and Unreal. The first group is what things are called, scene node, component, template, instance, override and data asset. These are the building blocks and how COP is relayed.

B0102.heard: The second group is how code runs and talks. Signal, Unity event, event dispatcher, and auto load. Then the language is GD script, C sharp, blueprint, and C++ and the clocks. These terms cover languages, loops, and messages.

B0103.heard: The third group is how things move and touch. Input action, character body, trigger, layer and mask, collision matrix and object type. These terms say how input arrives, what moves a body, and who notices whom.

B0104.heard: The fourth group is Space, Looks, and Shipping. Up-axis, units, clip, event key, state machine, shader, parameter, particles, export, and license. Access, animation, materials, and the build-you ship.

B0201.heard: A table with a column for each engine filling one row at a time. The first row is scene level map. A Godo scene, a unity scene, and an unreal level are each a saved reusable tree of objects and unreal calls its level file a map. A level is narrower, one playable space. For example, in Godo, the first level of a platformer is a scene file, and so is the coin placed in it, but only the first is a level.

B0202.heard: The second row is node, game object, actor, the name for one object in the scene. A node is Godo's object, and each node type already does one job. The Unity Game Object does nothing until components are added, and an Unreal actor also gains its behavior from components. For example, the player of a platformer is one character body 2D node in Godo, one game object in Unity, and one actor in Unreal.

B0203.heard: The third row is component, a piece of behavior or data attached to a game object or an actor. Godot has no component here. It picks a node type and adds child nodes instead. For example, a coin pickup in Unity is a game object with a collider component added and set as a trigger. In Godot, the same coin is an area 2D node with its collision shape as a child node.

B0204.heard: Now the same player drawn three ways. Red is the object itself. In Godo it is three nodes, one root and two filled child nodes. In Unity it is one game object with three outline components and an Unreal one actor with three components. The idea is the same and the shape is not. For example, when you ask an agent to port that player to Unity, ask for components on one game object, not a tree of child nodes.

B0301.heard: A single box at the top holds a speed of 160. A template is the master that copies come from. In Godot it is a scene in Unity A Pre-FAB and an Unreal or Blueprint class. Edit the template and the copies follow. For example, an enemy saved once as a template with its patrol speed inside can be placed all over a level, and every copy starts from that saved speed.

B0302.heard: Five boxes appear below it, each a copy holding 160. An instance is one copy made from a template and placed in the game. Edit an instance and only that copy changes. In Unity it is called a pre-fab instance. For example, the five enemies in your level are five instances of the one enemy template, so each can stand in its own spot with its own position.

B0303.heard: The template speed changes to 192 and 4 copies follow. Copy 3 keeps 200 because it holds an override, a change made on one instance. In Unity, Apply pushes an override back into the prefab and revert drops it. For example, you make one guard a castle gate faster than the rest. If you later want every guard that fast, you press Apply on that guard.

B0304.heard: Now one asset with three readers. A data asset is shared data kept as a file in the project, not in a scene. Godot calls it a resource, Unity a scriptable object, and Unreal a data asset. Here a player, a bot, and a menu take their speed from it, and one edit updates all three. For example, Walker keeps its run speed in a tuning resource, and a Unity version would keep it in a scriptable object asset.

B0401.heard: A ball exits and lines run to two listeners, score and sound. A signal is Godot's named event. Other nodes connect to it and run when it fires. Here it fires once and both listeners get the call 2 of 2. For example, in a Pong game the ball exited signal fires when the ball leaves the court, and the score counter and the goal sound both answer it.

B0402.heard: The same ball exit in Unity now with three listeners. Unity's events are the Unity event and the C-sharp event. The Unity event can be wired in the inspector, the editor panel, so that listener is stored in the scene file and not in any script. Here the UI listener was wired that way, three of three. For example, an agent that checks only the scripts of your Unity port can miss that the score text listens at all.

B0403.heard: Now Unreal, an event dispatcher is Unreal's blueprint form of a signal. You bind events to it and when call fires every bound event, in C++ the same job is done by a delegate. Here sound was bound twice, so its handler runs twice, three calls and all. For example, a coin whose sound handler was bound twice would play its pickup sound twice on a single touch.

B0404.heard: A new scene loads and six objects face it. Auto-load game instance names the things that outlive a scene. Godot uses an auto-load, unity calls don't destroy unload on a root object and unreal uses the game instance or a subsystem that shares its lifetime. The scorekeeper and the music are kept two of six. A signal is an announcement, and an auto-load is what is kept across scene changes, for example. Music that keeps playing from the menu into the first level needs one.

B0501.heard: Lanes from edit to run one per language. GD script is Godo's own scripting language, and its scripts are plain text files. Its lane has two stages, edit and run, because a change takes effect the next time Godo runs. Plain text also gives a diff, the lines that changed. For example, when an agent changes the jump height in a player script, you see the exact line in the diff and run the game straight away.

B0502.heard: C-sharp is Unity's language and Amano Behavior is a component script also playing text. Its lane adds a compile stage, 3 and all. Compile means turning code into a runnable form which is not the same as a diff, the lines that changed. For example, a Unity port of a coin script would be Amano Behavior on the coin's game object. You can diff it as text, but it must compile before the change runs.

B0503.heard: A blueprint graph is Unreal's visual scripting, boxes joined by wires. The graph is saved as a binary asset so an agent cannot diff it as text. Its lane has three stages with compile in the middle and it is marked binary. For example, if the run speed lives on a blueprint character, an agent cannot change it by editing a file. It has to work through the editor and you check the change in the editor's own diff tool.

B0504.heard: C++ and Unreal is the code route. It is plain text, so it gives a text diff, but it must be compiled before a change takes effect three stages again. That makes each try slower than in GD script. For example, an agent can set the player's default run speed in a C++ constructor and show you the diff, and then the project is compiled before you can test the new speed.

B0601.heard: Strips of tick marks across one second on a screen that draws a frame 144 times a second. In Go-Doh, the process function runs once per frame, so here 144 times. The physics process function runs at a fixed 60 times a second by default. The red marks 16.7 milliseconds apart. For example, a coin spin can go in the process function. While the players run and jump belong in the physics process function.

B0602.heard: Unity has the same two clocks under other names. Update runs once per frame, so the gap between calls can be any length. Fixed update runs at fixed steps of 0.02 seconds, which is 50 a second by default, not 60. For example, a test of a jump ported to Unity that counts physics steps over one second must expect 50 steps, not the 60 it counted in Godot.

B0603.heard: In Unreal, Tick is the per frame update. Each actor ticks every frame, so both lower strips show 144 ticks in the second. Tick groups such as Pre-Physics and Post-Physics order that work around the physics step. For example, an enemy actor's per frame logic runs in its tick, and placing it in the Pre-Physics group makes it run before the physics step in each frame.

B0701.heard: Three rows of key presses, one per engine. An input action is a named intent, such as jump, bound to keys, or buttons, and kept apart from them. Godo keeps it in the input map, unity in the input system, and unreal and enhanced input. Space in a gamepad button or bound and enter is not, so jump fires on three or four presses. For example, porting walkers jump means binding space to a jump action, not testing the space key in code.

B0702.heard: A character body is the body you move on purpose. In Godot it is a character body 2D that your script moves with move and slide. In Unity, a rigid body 2D stepped in fixed update, and an unreal a character whose movement component does the moving. Each dot covers 160 pixels in one second in 60, 50, or 144 steps. For example, Walker's player is a character body 2D. And in Unreal, its run speed would become the movement component's max walk speed.

B0703.heard: A trigger is a zone that reports overlaps instead of blocking, which a collider does. Godot uses an Area 2D. Unity a collider with his trigger ticked and unreal a trigger volume. The dot crosses the zone in one second and each engine reports the entry once. Unity also needs a rigid body 2D on one of the two objects and unreal needs generate overlap events on both, for example. Walker's goal flag is an Area 2D that notices the player without stopping it.

B0801.heard: A grid in which each row notices each column. Layer and mask is Godot's rule. Each object has a layer where it sits in a mask what it looks for. One object notices another if the other's layer is in its mask and that works one way. Here the player's mask holds mob and coin and they mask nothing, so two of six pairs notice. For example, in a dodge game the player detects the mobs while the mobs detect nothing.

B0802.heard: Unity uses a layer collision matrix. Each game object sits on one layer and one grid for the whole project says which pairs of layers collide. A tick works both ways, so ticking player with mob and player with coin makes four of six pairs notice. For example, the dodge game setup, where the player detects mobs that detect nothing, becomes a matrix setting in Unity, shared by every object on those layers.

B0803.heard: Unreal gives each object an object type in a response block, overlap, or ignore for every other type. Both sides must agree before contact happens. A mask is one side's filter and a response needs both. Here the mob answers ignore and does not generate overlap events so the player meets the mob with no event and no error. For example, if the creep in an Unreal Shield pickup game forgot to generate overlap events. The Shield check would silently stop working.

B0901.heard: Three axis drawings, one per engine, with the up axis in red. The up axis is the one that points up. Godo and Unity are y-up, so height is the y-value and unreal is z-up, so height is the z-value. Handedness is the other half of the setup. Unity and Unreal are left-handed, and Godo is right-handed. For example, in a 3D game, a jump that raises the player's y-value and Godo raises its z-value and unreal.

B0902.heard: The same post, 3 meters ahead and 1.8 meters up on two charts. In Unity it sits at 0, 1.83 meters. In Unreal it sits at 300, 0, 180 in centimeters. The map takes X from Z, Y from X and Z from Y, then multiplies by 100. For example, a checkpoint flag placed in a Unity level needs exactly this conversion before its position means anything in Unreal.

B0903.heard: Unit says how long one unit of distance is. In Godo and Unity, one unit is one meter. An unreal one unit is one centimeter. So the same post is 1.8 on one ruler and 180 on the other. The importer converts, but your expected numbers must change too. For example, a test that checks a doorway is 1.8 high now expects 180, and a tolerance of 0.05 meters becomes five.

B1001.heard: Three timelines, one per engine, each playing a clip half a second long. A clip is key data played over time, a value that changes from key to key and a player runs it. Godot uses an animation player with an animation, Unity an animator with an animation clip, an unreal animation sequence. Unity wraps even one clip in an animator controller. For example, a coin's half second bounce would be one clip in each engine.

B1002.heard: Keys now sit at 0.1 and 0.25 seconds. An event key is a call placed on the timeline, a method tracking go-dough, an animation event in Unity, and a notify an Unreal which fires at one time. An anim notify state, the red window, has a begin and an end. The hitbox stays on 0.15 seconds, nine steps at 60 hertz, eight at 50. For example, a sword swing switches its hitbox on and off this way.

B1003.heard: Three boxes joined by Arrow's idle, walk, and attack. A state machine is a set of states joined by transitions with rules, and the current state picks the clip. Here a speed above 0.1 moves idle to walk. Attack moves walk to attack, and attack finished returns to idle. Godot builds it in an animation tree, unity in an animator controller, and unreal in an anim blueprint, for example. A player sprite that plays its walk clip only while moving is driven by one.

B1101.heard: Where each engine defines how a surface looks, a shader is code that draws and a material holds the settings it reads. Godo and Unity write shaders as code or as a graph. Unreal builds materials as node graphs in the Material Editor with a custom node for HLSL, the high-level shading language. Unreal's material is a binary asset and the other two can be plain text. For example, a flash shader on a Godo sprite is a text file an agent can edit.

B1102.heard: One flash value is set from code in each engine, and the swatches fade to gray as it falls to zero. Material parameter is a named value that your code sets and the shader reads. Godot calls it a uniform set on a shader material. Unity sets a material property or a material property block for one object. Unreal sets a scalar parameter on a dynamic material instance. For example, an enemy that flashes when hit sets its flash value high. Then lets it fall.

B1103.heard: In this ceded simulation, 32 particles burst from one point. A particle system is many small sprites simulated together. Godot uses GPU particles, unity the VFX graph, and Unreal Niagara. A one-shot burst spawns them all at once, and with one shared lifetime of 0.6 seconds, all 32 end together. For example, the sparks when the player grabs a coin can be a one-shot burst that plays once and is gone.

B1201.heard: Three build commands typed out. Build and export means packaging the project for a platform. Godot saves export presets and needs one flag on the editor. Unity 6 saves a build profile and your script calls its build pipeline. Unreal packages the project and cooks it, converting every asset for the target so export and cook are different steps. For example, shipping your platformer for the web from Godot starts from a saved web export preset.

B1202.heard: License means the terms you build and sell under. GoDo is MIT licensed with no royalty. Unity is proprietary, and its personal plan holds only while 12-month finances stay at or under $200,000. Unreal is source available, not open source, with a 5% royalty above the first million dollars per product. For example, in this illustrative case, a game grosses $1.5 million, and owes nothing under GoDo in $25,000 under Unreal.

B1301.heard: Each pair sets two look-alike ideas side by side. Edit the template and every copy without an override changes three of three. Edit an instance and only that copy changes one of three.

B1302.heard: Y up against Z up and Go-Doh in unity height is Y in meters so the dot rises to 1.8 and unreal height is Z in centimeters so the same dot rises to 180.

B1303.heard: Update against fixed update. Update runs once per frame, so the gaps vary 39 frames in a quarter second here. Fixed update runs every 0.02 seconds in Unity, however many frames pass 13 steps.

B1304.heard: A Godo mask against an unreal response. In Godo, one object notices another when the other's layer is in its mask, so one side decides. In Unreal, both sides must answer overlap or block. Here the second object says ignore, so nothing happens.

B1401.heard: Each vague request becomes an exact instruction. Convert it for Unreal becomes, map the Unity point with X from Z, Y from X and Z from Y times 100. The answer is 300, 0, 180. Y is 0 so the post is straight ahead.

B1402.heard: Run it at the right rate becomes, Godot runs physics 60 times a second in Unity's fixed update 50, so count steps. That is 16.7 milliseconds a step against 20, and 10 fewer steps a second in Unity.

B1403.heard: Make the pickup fire becomes, and Unity Tick is trigger and give one of the two objects a rigid body 2D. Of the four combinations of those two settings, only one fires, the one with both.

B1404.heard: Make the mob see the player becomes, and Unreal both actors answer overlap and turn on generate overlap events. Again only one of four settings fires, overlap yes and events on yes.

B1405.heard: Update every enemy becomes edit the template. Four of five copies change to 192 and the one with an override keeps its 200. An override beats the template.

B1501.heard: A checklist of six questions to ask before you port an idea between engines. First, am I using this engine's word, node, game object, or actor?

B1502.heard: Second, which clock does the code need? Per frame or the fixed step? 60 a second in Go-Doh and 50 in Unity.

B1503.heard: Third, which way is up, Y or Z, and are the units meters or centimeters? Get either one wrong and every position in the level is off.

B1504.heard: Fourth does contact work from one side as with a go-dough mask or do both sides have to agree as with an unreal response.

B1505.heard: Fifth is the asset text that you can diff, like a Godo scene or a C-sharp script or binary, like a blueprint, that you must open the editor for.

B1506.heard: Sixth, was it run or only looked up in documentation? Neither unity nor unreal was run for these comparisons. Then say it exactly. Not make it work in unity, but tick is trigger and add a rigid body to D.

BVDT.heard: Let's recap, a Godot node maps to a Unity game object and an Unreal actor. Edit the template and copies follow, but an override keeps its own value. A blueprint graph is binary so an agent cannot diff it as text. Godot's fixed step runs 60 times a second, Unity's fixed update 50. A Godot mask works one way and an Unreal response needs both sides. Godot and Unity are Y up in meters and Unreal is Z up in centimeters.

BHTF.heard: Quizmy I'm porting a Godo game to Unity and Unreal with short game-making cases one at a time. Use the terms GameObject Actor Pre-FAB Override Scriptable Object Event Dispatcher fixed update Layer Collision Matrix Object Type and ZUp. For each case I must name the exact term in the right engine and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply.

BOUT.heard: Key terms go doe unity and unreal at Nick Bear Brown.
